quick: 1 mg start, titrate to 6-10 mg/day in divided doses
Before meals if dry mouth; after meals if nausea
Category C; use only if needed
summary: Trihexyphenidyl is a centrally acting anticholinergic used as adjunct in parkinsonism and to control drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms. Started low (1 mg) and titrated gradually to 6-10 mg/day. Key cautions are narrow-angle glaucoma, anticholinergic toxicity and use in the elderly.
indications: Adjunct in the treatment of all forms of parkinsonism (postencephalitic, arteriosclerotic, idiopathic)
Adjuvant therapy with levodopa in parkinsonism
Control of extrapyramidal disorders caused by CNS drugs (dibenzoxazepines, phenothiazines, thioxanthenes, butyrophenones)

dosage.d: Start 1 mg day 1; increase by 2 mg every 3-5 days to 6-10 mg/day

admin: Individualize dose; start low and increase gradually
Take before meals if drug causes excessive dry mouth, unless it causes nausea
Take after meals if it causes nausea (postencephalitic patients with excess salivation)
Do not withdraw abruptly to avoid acute exacerbation of parkinsonism
Sustained-release capsules are for maintenance only, not initiation
moa: Blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in the central nervous system, restoring the balance between dopaminergic and cholinergic activity in the basal ganglia. This central antimuscarinic action relieves rigidity and tremor in parkinsonism and counteracts drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms; it also has direct antispasmodic effect on smooth muscle.
preg: Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted; it is not known whether it can cause fetal harm. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Use with caution; anticholinergics may suppress lactation. Generally avoided during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution; no specific dose adjustment defined, but reduced clearance may increase anticholinergic effects.
hepatic: Use with caution; no specific dose adjustment defined.

major: Other anticholinergics (antihistamines, TCAs, antipsychotics) - additive anticholinergic toxicity
Potassium chloride solid oral - increased GI lesion risk from delayed transit
moderate: Phenothiazines - reduced antipsychotic levels and increased anticholinergic effects
Levodopa - may reduce gastric emptying and absorption
interactions.food: No significant food interaction; timing relative to meals adjusted for tolerability.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive CNS depression and sedation.
interactions.diagnostics: May reduce gastric motility and mask GI obstruction.

monitoring: Gonioscopy and intraocular pressure before and during therapy
counsel: Report eye pain or visual changes promptly (glaucoma risk)
Use caution in hot weather; risk of overheating
Do not stop the drug suddenly
Use sugar-free gum or sips of water for dry mouth
pk: Store at controlled room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: More effective against rigidity and tremor than bradykinesia
Useful for drug-induced parkinsonism but not for tardive dyskinesia
Avoid abrupt withdrawal; taper to prevent rebound
High anticholinergic burden - use cautiously in the elderly
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. Resume the regular schedule.
overdose: Produces an anticholinergic toxidrome (dry flushed skin, hyperthermia, dilated pupils, delirium, tachycardia, urinary retention). Treat with supportive care, cooling, and physostigmine for severe central toxicity; control seizures and agitation.
